lane: orientation and tip heads with geometry-aware decoding (parallel-run lane brief)
hypothesis: Fault geometry (axial strike and tip/junction structure) learned jointly with per-pixel evidence (Batra et al. CVPR 2019 multi-branch heads, adapted to undirected faults as cos 2theta/sin 2theta) decodes to line networks with better topology than per-pixel classification alone, and orientation-consistent extension past mapped tips recovers fault segments missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue because mapped tips are systematically short (tip zones below mapping resolution: ~500 m per fault in one published seismic array; 100-200 m DEM truncation in a rift study).
mechanism: A segmentation head (logistic, 26 catalogue-free GeoDAWN fabric layers) supplies probability; an axial orientation head (ridge regression to (cos 2t, sin 2t) of visible-trace geometry within 3 px) supplies strike; a tip head (Gaussian sigma 1.5 px heat at visible-trace endpoints and junctions) supplies stop/continue cues. Decoding: orientation-gated hysteresis (|dtheta| <= 45 deg to the nearest seed axis), orientation-aware NMS (thin along the predicted normal, bilinear sampling), then <= 6 px (600 m) tip marches along outward strike while probability support persists. Candidates within 2 px of the mapped catalogue are flank-pruned (h33 lesson) with extension pixels protected; nodes are selected by the shared greedy marginal-DTI allocator (k_truth prior 45,000 px, preregistered).
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Fluvial terrace risers and channel-bank lines (coherent strike, tip-like endings); landslide headscarps; playa shorelines and evaporite fronts (conductivity contrast); roads and canals; lithologic contacts in the potential-field bands (coherent edges with no fault throw).
